_Verified against the running system on 2026-09-04._

# Acceptance criteria verification


[ MET ] 1.1 single repository for manual and automated cases
         25,002 managed cases, 2001 automated and 23001 not, in one repository
[ MET ] 1.2 organised by product, component, module, release stream, test level, workflow
         suite tree of 45 nodes for product/component/module, plus 11 tags for the remaining axes (design Decision 2)
[ MET ] 1.3 metadata: ownership, priority, risk, tags, preconditions, steps, expected results, automation status
         all eight present on EXA-1000
[ MET ] 1.4 versioning or change history
         11 history entries on EXA-1000, each with actor, timestamp and originating interface
[ MET ] 1.5 retention clearly defined and tied to managed assets
         12-month window; applies to execution history: runs, results, step results, defect links, attachments; excludes managed test assets: cases, suites, shared steps, plans, and their history
[ MET ] 1.6 results exportable or accessible externally
         streaming CSV export (text/csv; charset=utf-8), plus a paginated REST endpoint

[ MET ] 2.1 native integration or clear path for GitHub Actions
         documented workflow in docs/ci/github-actions.md, verified against the running instance
[ MET ] 2.2 headless upload via CLI or script
         single curl with a bearer token; no client library to install
[ MET ] 2.3 Pytest, Playwright, JUnit XML supported
         one JUnit XML parser covers both; tested against real pytest and Playwright output (21 tests)
[ MET ] 2.4 automated tests map to cases via stable identifiers
         100,904 bindings: 100,604 by declared case id, 300 by name; 45 reported stale
[ MET ] 2.5 scoped API tokens for CI
         project-scoped, scope-limited, revocable, stored only as a hash
[ MET ] 2.6 practical for mixed execution environments
         3 environments; any runner that can POST integrates

[ MET ] 3.1 shows which cases are automated vs manual vs untested
         2,001 automated / 23 manual / 22,978 never executed, summing to 25,002
[ MET ] 3.2 coverage across integration, e2e, performance, security categories
         grouped by tag into 12 categories, including an explicit untagged group
[ MET ] 3.3 coverage filterable by product, module, feature, release
         filters by suite subtree, tag, custom field and release; verified by 14 integration tests

[ MET ] 4.1 release-level view of execution progress
         91.2% pass across 10 run(s)
[PART.] 4.2 open defects with breakdowns such as severity and age
         defect links listed with age since linking (0 linked), but severity and open/closed state are not read back — Jira is link-only (design Decision 5)
[ MET ] 4.3 blocking failures, critical issues, coverage gaps, UAT status, gate in one place
         blocking 340, known 0, coverage 400/400, UAT 3/3, gate signed off
[PART.] 4.4 dashboard sufficient for a confident go/no-go
         every decision input is present and was exercised in the rehearsal; the gate records approvals rather than computing a verdict from evidence (design Decision 16)

[ MET ] 5.1 structured manual runs for UAT and release validation
         12 manual/UAT runs
[ MET ] 5.2 testers attach evidence to steps or runs
         attachments stored in MinIO, retrievable under the same project permissions; oversized uploads refused with a clear limit
[ NOT ] 5.3 engineers inspect evidence from automated runs
         JUnit XML carries no attachment mechanism, so automated runs produce no evidence to inspect (design Decision 8)
[ MET ] 5.4 defect created from a failed step and linked to Jira
         issue key recorded against the failing step, rendered as a Jira link; validated against the key format
[ MET ] 5.5 efficient for repeated cycles and business users
         plans make a selection reusable; execution is keyboard-driven; per-project roles scope a business user to one project

[ MET ] 6.1 ingestion without manual approval or reconciliation
         the run is created automatically on upload; no approval step exists
[ MET ] 6.2 imported results update the triage flow automatically
         500 triaged signatures; a matching failure inherits its prior state, verified in the rehearsal

[PART.] 7.1 pass rate, failure rate, runtime, coverage, flakiness, open bugs
         pass 91.6%, failure 8.4%, runtime p50 1530ms, coverage 2001/25002, 60 flaky candidates, 1 defect age bands. Flakiness is cross-run only; defect *escapees* and severity need Jira state, which is not read back
[ MET ] 7.2 dashboard and trend views for recurring review
         30 days of trend data, bounded by the 12-month retention window and stated as such

[ MET ] 8.1 cases, executions and defect data via a documented API
         17 MCP tools plus 68 documented REST routes, generated from the live route table
[ MET ] 8.2 access controlled with security and permission boundaries
         MCP resolves the same per-project role through the same authorisation function as the web interface; no second permission path
[ MET ] 8.3 MCP support to interact with the tool
         JSON-RPC endpoint at /mcp with read and write tools, enforcing the caller role

[ NOT ] 9.1 OAuth or compatible security
         local accounts with JWT sessions; OIDC is deferred behind an AuthProvider interface (design Decision 7)
[ MET ] 9.2 practical RBAC for different user groups
         per-project roles (admin/lead/tester/viewer) resolved from data, with no account privileged by identity

28 met, 3 partially met, 2 not met (of 33)
